claim: This paper (v1) was self-withdrawn by its author with the stated reason that empirical validation in Sections 5-7 is insufficient to support the paper's global-applicability claims; only the theoretical model (Section 3) is still defended by the author.
stance_target: reliability/citability of this paper's empirical crowding and tail-risk findings
quoted_support: Withdrawal for major revision. Further analysis revealed that empirical validation in Sections 5-7 is insufficient to support the global applicability claims. The theoretical contributions remain valid. A revised version is in preparation.

claim: Judgment-based factors (value/HML, quality/RMW, investment/CMA) show essentially no fit to any tested alpha-decay model (R-squared of 0.05, 0.05, and 0.01 respectively, 1995-2024), in sharp contrast to momentum (R^2=0.65 hyperbolic fit) and long-term reversal (R^2=0.30) -- the paper's proposed explanation is a 'mechanical vs judgment' taxonomy where mechanical/unambiguous signals crowd predictably and judgment-based signals (with multiple valid implementations) do not.
stance_target: the assumption that quality-factor crowding follows the same predictable decay/crowding dynamics as momentum or other mechanical factors
scope_conditions: 8 Fama-French factors, 1963-2024 (fit window 1995-2024), US equities; caveat: paper self-withdrawn for insufficient empirical validation
quoted_support: judgment-based factors (HML, RMW, CMA) show poor fits across all models (R2 < 0.10)... Mechanical factors achieve mean R2 = 0.37; judgment factors achieve mean R2 = 0.04—an order of magnitude lower.

claim: Out-of-sample (2001-2024), crowded reversal factors show 1.65-1.84x higher crash probability than uncrowded states, while crowded momentum shows LOWER crash risk (0.38x, p=0.006) -- crowding predicts tail risk asymmetrically depending on whether the factor is trend-following (momentum, benign when crowded) or mean-reverting (reversal, dangerous when crowded), because trend-following crowding reinforces the prevailing trend while mean-reversion crowding bets against it.
stance_target: an undifferentiated claim that 'crowding is dangerous' applied equally to all crowded factors/strategies including momentum-driven mega-cap quality names
scope_conditions: 8 Fama-French factors, out-of-sample 2001-2024, US equities; caveat: paper self-withdrawn, this is exactly the type of empirical result (Sections 5-7) the author flagged as insufficiently validated
quoted_support: crowded reversal factors show 1.7-1.8x higher crash probability... while crowded momentum shows lower crash risk (0.38x, p = 0.006)... Trend-following (momentum): Crowding confirms trend strength -> lower crash risk. Mean-reverting (reversal): Crowding bets against trend -> higher crash risk if trend continues.

claim: Crowding-based factor-timing trading strategies underperform a naive factor-momentum benchmark (Sharpe 0.22 vs 0.39, 2017-2025), and 7 of 8 tested factors were flagged as crowded by the model's real-time signal -- suggesting crowding information is efficiently priced into average returns even though it may still carry tail-risk information.
stance_target: whether observable crowding metrics can be traded on directly for excess average returns
scope_conditions: 8 Fama-French factors, 2017-2025 out-of-sample trading test; caveat: paper self-withdrawn
quoted_support: Factor Momentum (0.39) outperforms both crowding-timed (0.22) and equal weight (0.17)... Our evidence is most consistent with H2—crowding is observable but efficiently priced.

claim: The over-prediction of momentum's remaining alpha post-2015 (model predicted 0.30, actual 0.15) correlates strongly with factor-ETF trading-volume growth (Pearson rho = -0.63, p<0.001, 2013-2024), consistent with ETF-driven democratization of factor investing accelerating crowding beyond historically calibrated rates.
stance_target: passive/ETF flows as an accelerant of factor crowding beyond fundamentals-driven equilibrium
scope_conditions: US factor ETFs, 2013-2024; caveat: paper self-withdrawn
quoted_support: Finding: Pearson rho = -0.63 (p < 0.001). The negative correlation indicates that as ETF volume grows, the model increasingly over-predicts remaining alpha.
